title: Fresh Peach Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Lightly cooked peach purée stirred into a lighter custard; less vanilla.
summary: Our classic French custard, made a little lighter and finished with a lightly cooked fresh peach purée. Summery, soft and full of fruit.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the peaches
steps.text: Chop the peaches and cook them with 50 g sugar and the lemon juice in the small pan for 6-8 min until soft and juicy. Blend to a slightly chunky purée and chill; brief cooking drives off some water and keeps the ice cream from turning icy.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Warm the cream, milk and salt until steaming. Whisk the yolks with 90 g sugar, temper with two ladles of the hot dairy and pour back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook to temperature
steps.text: Stir over low heat until it coats the spatula and reads 77-80 °C. Keep it below a simmer so it stays smooth.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Sieve, add the vanilla, cool over the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Combine and churn
steps.text: Stir in the cold peach purée and churn until thick. Both parts must be cold so the machine freezes them quickly.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze for at least 4 h, and eat within a week for the best fruit flavour.

tips: Peel peaches easily by scoring a cross in the base and dipping them in boiling water for 30 seconds.
A common mistake is using hard, underripe peaches, which have little flavour. Use fragrant ones that give slightly when pressed.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 1 week. Soften for 10 min before scooping, as fruit ice creams set harder.
